content: Doxylamine is an antihistamine that induces drowsiness as a side effect. It is primarily prescribed for the short-term treatment of insomnia. Additionally, it is used in combination with decongestants to alleviate symptoms of cough and cold. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Doxylamine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For insomnia, it is typically taken 30 minutes before bedtime. For cold symptoms, it is usually taken every 4 to 6 hours. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take doxylamine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Do not administer doxylamine to children under 12 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking doxylamine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to doxylamine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, muscle relaxation, pain relief, sedation, sleep, or anxiety, as well as any vitamins. Do not take doxylamine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, lung disease, glaucoma, ulcers, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate), heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking doxylamine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking doxylamine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. Doxylamine may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take it with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Doxylamine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dryness of the mouth, nose, and throat. If this symptom is severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include vision problems, difficulty urinating, muscle weakness, excitement, or nervousness. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store doxylamine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
